Is the total 75 or more? Give the total in the evidence.

summaries.gardner: ADI is a top dog in high-performance analog chips with a durable advantage and strong momentum (shares up about 66% over 52 weeks), but it is a 1965-founded leader of a mature, cyclical industry that ordinary people do not know. It fits Rule Breaker investing only partly, mainly through its fast-growing AI data-center and edge-AI ventures.
summaries.buffett: ADI has a wide moat from switching costs and design know-how, converts profit into ample free cash flow ($4,278.7M in FY2025), has raised its dividend for 22 straight years and commits to return 100% of free cash flow over time. Against that, results are cyclical (FY2024 revenue fell 23%), returns on capital are only about 11% because of acquisition goodwill, debt exceeds cash, and at about 47 times trailing earnings there is no margin of safety.
summaries.munger: Munger would value ADI's hard-to-copy analog know-how, sticky design-ins and rational capital returns. Inverting, the main ways to lose are a cyclical downturn after the 2026 boom, Chinese competition and overpaying, and a trailing P/E near 47 leaves little room for error.
summaries.lynch: ADI is a cyclical stalwart with a simple story: chips that measure and power the physical world, now in a strong upswing (nine-month FY2026 revenue up 36%). Lynch would note the forward P/E of about 25 is roughly in line with expected growth, while the share count is shrinking but the CEO sells shares regularly rather than buying.
summaries.fisher: ADI fits Fisher well on long-term research (about $1.7B a year), a steady flow of new products into new markets like AI power delivery and edge AI, deep customer relationships and conservative management. Weaker points are GAAP margins that were lower in FY2025 than FY2020 and growth that depends heavily on acquisitions and the chip cycle.
summaries.graham: ADI passes Graham's size, ten-year profitability, 20+ years of dividends and ten-year EPS growth tests (diluted EPS $2.20 in FY2015 to $4.56 in FY2025), and its current ratio is about 1.25. It clearly fails his price tests at about 47 times trailing earnings and 5.7 times book value.
summaries.thiel: ADI is a leader in many small high-performance niches with real secrets in analog design and a strong distribution and field-engineering network, but its technology is not ten times better than rivals' like Texas Instruments and it competes in an established, crowded market rather than a monopoly it created.
summaries.gerstner: Gerstner would like the sharp upturn (Q3 FY2026 revenue +40%), rising estimates, five straight earnings beats and growing exposure to AI data centers through communications and power delivery. He would question a trailing P/E near 47 and whether ADI is a true AI platform winner or a cyclical beneficiary.
summaries.druckenmiller: The setup Druckenmiller looks for is largely present: accelerating earnings, upward estimate revisions, reported price increases and strong price momentum. The risk is that much of the cyclical recovery is already priced in and the cycle could turn within his 18-24 month horizon.
summaries.smith: ADI meets Terry Smith's quality tests on gross margin (61.5% in FY2025, 67.3% in Q3 FY2026) and cash conversion, and its products are hard to displace. It falls short on return on capital (about 11% because of large acquisition goodwill) and on 'don't overpay' at a free-cash-flow yield near 2.6%.
summaries.greenblatt: ADI does not screen well on the Magic Formula: its return on tangible capital is decent, but its earnings yield is low, with trailing operating income of about $4.9B against an enterprise value near $198B (about 2.5%).
summaries.akre: ADI has a good business and a capable long-serving management team, two legs of Akre's stool, but reinvestment at high rates is the weak leg: it pays out most free cash flow and has grown mainly through large acquisitions, and returns on capital are only around 11%.
summaries.pabrai: ADI is a high-quality, low-risk business, but it is not a Dhandho bet: there is no distress, no deep discount and no 'heads I win, tails I don't lose much' setup at about 47 times trailing earnings.
summaries.wood: ADI supplies key enablers for robotics, electrification and AI infrastructure and is moving into edge-AI processors (Alif deal), but it is an incumbent component maker rather than a disruptive platform with rapidly falling costs, so it is only a partial fit with ARK's approach.
summaries.ackman: ADI fits several of Ackman's criteria: simple, predictable, free-cash-flow-generative, with high barriers to entry and a strong balance sheet relative to cash flow. It is less attractive on price, and there is no obvious activist angle at a well-run company.
summaries.sleep: ADI does not show Nomad-style scale economics shared with customers; it reportedly raised prices in 2026. Its sticky design-ins and long horizons appeal, but its future strength rests on product leadership rather than a self-reinforcing cost advantage.
summaries.valentine: ADI addresses large, important problems (sensing and powering machines, cars and data centers) in growing markets, which Valentine valued, but it is a mature 60-year-old company, so his startup-focused lens on market timing and new markets applies only partly.
summaries.nash: ADI scores very highly on Nash's quality categories (revenue growth, operating margin above 35% on a trailing basis, low short interest, high institutional ownership) and sells into AI, robotics and electrification. It fails his instant-kill rule because debt ($9,121.6M) exceeds cash ($2,324.9M), and his DCF does not support today's price at a 12% discount rate.

momentum.evidence: ADI closed at $395.44 on October 16, 2026, up about 66% over 52 weeks, far ahead of the S&P 500.

g4.evidence: Long-serving CEO Vincent Roche (CEO since 2013) has a solid record, and institutions own about 92% of shares, but no famous investor or strategic partner stands behind it.

g6.evidence: At about 47 times trailing earnings some commentators call ADI expensive, but most analysts rate it a buy (24 of 34 strong buy) with an average target of $471.34.

simple.evidence: The basic business, selling chips that sense, convert and power real-world signals, is understandable, but judging its 75,000 products and technology position takes industry knowledge.

b2.evidence: ADI has been profitable for decades and raised its dividend 22 years running, but results swing with the chip cycle, e.g. FY2024 revenue fell 23% to $9,427.2M before rebounding.

integrity.evidence: ADI gives clear quarterly guidance it has beaten five quarters in a row, commits to returning 100% of free cash flow over the long term, and has a clean governance record, though Roche is both CEO and Chair.

b6.evidence: ADI has grown through large deals (Hittite 2014, Linear Technology 2017, Maxim 2022) that were strategic rather than empire-building, but acquisitions remain a central part of its playbook, including Empower (2026) and Alif (pending).

roic.evidence: Return on invested capital is about 11% on a trailing basis because of $27,988.7M of goodwill from acquisitions, though returns on tangible capital are high and debt is modest versus cash flow.

fcf.evidence: FY2025 free cash flow was $4,278.7M (39% of revenue), well above net income of $2,267.3M, and trailing free cash flow reached $4,937.5M by August 2026.

b10.evidence: ADI pays out most cash flow, and value creation from retained capital has come mostly via acquisitions such as Maxim, which added scale but diluted returns on capital.

safety.evidence: At $395.44, about 47 times trailing GAAP EPS of $8.42 and 39 times free cash flow, the price is not below a conservative value estimate.

fairprice.evidence: The forward P/E of about 25 (PEG about 0.9) looks reasonable for a cyclical upswing, but the trailing P/E near 47 and free-cash-flow yield of 2.6% are demanding.

mu5.evidence: ADI's diversified base of 100,000+ customers makes failure unlikely, but cyclical downturns, China competition and export controls could sharply cut earnings.

reinvest.evidence: Organic reinvestment (about $1.7B of R&D yearly) earns good returns, but ADI cannot deploy most of its cash flow internally and returns it to shareholders or buys companies.

ly2.evidence: ADI is a cyclical stalwart: a leading analog chip maker currently in an upswing, with nine-month FY2026 revenue up 36% to $10,805.6M.

ly3.evidence: The trailing P/E of about 47 is above long-term growth, but the forward P/E of about 25 is below expected near-term EPS growth (PEG about 0.89).

runway.evidence: AI data-center power and networking, robotics, electrification and edge AI (Empower acquired July 2026, Alif announced September 2026) give ADI new markets to grow into for years.

ly7.evidence: Diluted shares fell from 496.7M in FY2025 to 488.8M in Q3 FY2026 after $2,446.4M of nine-month buybacks, but the CEO has been selling about 10,000 shares at a time rather than buying.

ly8.evidence: ADI is a large, widely covered S&P 500 company with 34 analysts setting price targets.

fi2.evidence: ADI keeps pushing into new areas as older ones mature, such as AI processor power delivery and AI microcontrollers through the Empower and Alif acquisitions.

fi3.evidence: Its roughly $1.7B yearly R&D supports leadership in precision converters and battery-management chips and a catalogue of about 75,000 products with about 8,000 patents.

fi4.evidence: ADI's large field-applications-engineering force and distribution reach more than 100,000 customers, a real selling strength, though not unusually better than Texas Instruments'.

longterm.evidence: Management invests through cycles in R&D and capacity and frames strategy over decades around the Intelligent Edge and Physical Intelligence.

gr1.evidence: ADI has a market value of about $192B and FY2025 revenue of $11,019.7M.

ni10.evidence: ADI has been profitable in each of the last ten fiscal years, earning $2,267.3M in FY2025 and $1,635.3M even in the FY2024 downturn.

gr4.evidence: ADI has paid dividends since its capital return program began 22 years ago and raised the dividend for 22 consecutive years, most recently 11% to $1.10 a quarter in February 2026.

eps10.evidence: Diluted EPS rose from $2.20 in FY2015 to $4.56 in FY2025, a gain of about 107%.

gr6.evidence: The share price of $395.44 is about 47 times trailing EPS of $8.42 and far above 15 times average earnings over FY2023-FY2025 ($6.55, $3.28 and $4.56).

gr7.evidence: P/E of about 47 times P/B of about 5.7 gives roughly 268, far above Graham's 22.5 limit.

th1.evidence: ADI's chips lead in precision and performance in many niches, but rivals such as Texas Instruments and Infineon offer close alternatives, not ten-times-worse ones.

timing.evidence: The chip cycle has turned up and AI data-center demand is surging, with Q3 FY2026 communications revenue up 84% and industrial up 53% year on year.

th3.evidence: ADI built leadership in small high-performance analog niches like data converters and expanded across industrial, automotive and communications, but that happened decades ago.

team.evidence: Vincent Roche is an experienced, effective CEO who grew revenue from $2.7B in FY2012 to $11.0B in FY2025, but he is not a founder or a widely celebrated leader.

th5.evidence: ADI reaches 100,000+ customers through direct field engineers, distributors and online design tools, a distribution system rivals cannot easily copy.

durable.evidence: The physical world will keep needing analog sensing and power conversion, and ADI's 60-year design know-how and long design-in cycles make its position hard to disrupt.

th7.evidence: ADI's 'Physical Intelligence' push to combine analog sensing with edge AI processing is distinctive but is also being pursued by rivals like TI, NXP and Infineon.

trend.evidence: ADI benefits from AI data-center build-outs (communications revenue up 84% in Q3 FY2026), automation and electrification, but it is a supplier of supporting chips rather than the leading beneficiary.

dr1.evidence: Quarterly GAAP EPS rose from $1.04 in Q3 FY2025 to $2.74 in Q3 FY2026, and consensus FY2026 revenue has risen to about $15.1B with FY2027 at $18.31B.

dr2.evidence: Price increases, AI power delivery and a closed Alif deal could make ADI look better, but the strong upswing is already widely known and priced into a trailing P/E near 47.

dr4.evidence: ADI's industrial and automotive demand benefits from a growing economy and easier money, but higher rates or a slowdown would hit its cyclical end markets.

dr6.evidence: Catalysts include Q4 FY2026 results against guidance of $4.3B revenue, reported price increases, and closing of the $1.35B Alif acquisition expected before end of 2026.

dr7.evidence: ADI's quality supports a sizable holding, but cyclical risk and a full valuation argue against a highly concentrated position.

gm.evidence: GAAP gross margin was 61.5% in FY2025 and rose to 67.3% in Q3 FY2026, among the highest for analog chip makers.

fcfyield.evidence: Free-cash-flow yield is about 2.6% (P/FCF about 39), modest for a cyclical but acceptable given current growth above 30%.

gb2.evidence: Trailing operating income of about $4,934.9M is only about 2.5% of the roughly $198B enterprise value.

pa2.evidence: ADI is not in a setback; its FY2024 downturn has already given way to record revenue in Q3 FY2026.

pa4.evidence: The business is very unlikely to be impaired, but at about 47 times trailing earnings a cyclical downturn could cause a large, lasting drop in the share price.

wo1.evidence: ADI supplies sensing, motor-control and power chips for robotics and AI data centers and is buying edge-AI chip maker Alif, but it is an enabler rather than a recognized AI or robotics leader.

wo4.evidence: ADI's markets are large and growing but are not likely to be many times larger within five years.

ns1.evidence: ADI uses its position to raise prices (reported average increase of about 15% from February 2026) rather than passing scale savings to customers.

ns4.evidence: New AI power and edge-AI businesses could strengthen ADI, but its core analog position is already mature and faces rising Chinese competition.

va2.evidence: ADI solves the painful problem of accurately measuring, converting and powering real-world signals in cars, factories, medical devices and AI data centers.

tn1.evidence: ADI sells infrastructure-layer chips into AI data centers, robotics and electrification, but it is a 1965-founded analog company adapting to these trends rather than one built for them.

tn10.evidence: There is no major lawsuit, but US-China export controls, tariffs and antitrust review of acquisitions are ongoing regulatory risks.

tn11.evidence: ADI provides analog, mixed-signal and power chips that help equipment makers sense, measure, connect and power their systems accurately, charging per chip sold, and engineers pick it for best-in-class precision and support.
